newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK handover legislature passes law curbing rights.
newsitem.headline: HK handover legislature passes law curbing rights.

text.p: Hong Kong's future legislature passed a law on Saturday curbing political freedoms when the British-ruled territory reverts to China on July 1, Hong Kong Cable Television said.
The Provisional Legislature adopted an amendment to Hong Kong's Public Order Ordinance at a session in China's Shenzhen city, curbing the right of assembly and protest, the station said.
The 60-member provisional body, filled with pro-Beijing politicians and tycoons, will replace Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council (Legco) at the handover.

The provisional lawmakers were also set to adopt an amendment to Hong Kong's Societies Ordinance, the law that covers the formation of political parties. That change is intended to bar foreign funding of political groups.
The West has criticised Beijing for replacing Legco with the provisional legislature, whose 400 members were hand-picked by China in a move that effectively scrapped the colony's democratic reforms.
China takes back Hong Kong after 156 years of British colonial rule.
